verdict.summary: Composio has no managed bexio app, so you have to register your own. That is self-serve: log into developer.bexio.com with a bexio account (a free trial works), accept the terms, create an app and add the redirect URL. No bexio page we found mentions a review step or user cap for OAuth apps. The commercial-use rules (Section 4.4) reportedly require you to tell bexio once at least five bexio accounts are connected. Review only applies if you want a Marketplace listing, which has strict entry requirements.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min (plus a few days of work if you apply for a Marketplace listing)
verdict.approval_wait: none documented for OAuth apps; Marketplace listing review has no published timeline

gates.name: Developer app (your own account)
gates.unlocks: You can connect your own bexio company through Composio using your app's client ID and secret.
limits: Needs a bexio account. The 30-day free trial is enough.
Up to 10 redirect URLs per app
Access is limited to the connecting user's own bexio permissions

gates.unlocks: Other bexio users can authorize your app. No bexio page we found mentions a test-user allowlist, install cap or approval step.

Offline (refresh-token) sessions expire after 1 year idle

gates.unlocks: Anyone can connect without review (bexio says API access is not restricted). A Marketplace listing adds discovery inside bexio, but it requires a partner application and a partner agreement.
limits: Separate client ID/secret recommended for production
Marketplace only: at least 10 bexio customers among your regular clients and at least 20 active users of your app
Marketplace only: OpenID Connect login required; app in at least 2 of DE/FR/IT/EN; listing content in all 4 languages
Marketplace only: 25% service fee on revenue from shared users (20% for top partners), bexio collects payments directly, price parity required, you provide end-user support
gates.time_to_reach: Public use: immediate (bexio recommends a separate production app). Marketplace: no published timeline.

steps.title: Get a bexio account
steps.detail: Sign in to bexio, or start the free 30-day trial at bexio.com. This account will own the developer app.
gotchas: Keep the account active after the trial ends if production apps depend on it.

steps.title: Log into the developer portal and accept the terms
steps.detail: Go to developer.bexio.com, log in with your bexio credentials and accept the portal terms. Read the commercial-use rules in Section 4.4 carefully.
gotchas: Section 4.4 reportedly requires you to inform bexio once at least 5 bexio accounts are connected to your own business model.

steps.title: Create the app and register the redirect URL
steps.detail: Create a new app in the developer portal and add the Composio callback URL as an allowed redirect URL. You can add up to 10 redirect URLs.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Authorization fails with an error for any redirect URL that is not registered. Paste the callback URL exactly as shown.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and secret
steps.detail: Open 'App Details' for the app and copy the client ID and client secret. The secret is used at the server-side token exchange, so keep it only in Composio or on your server.
gotchas: Never put the client secret in browser or mobile code.

steps.title: Pick a minimal scope list
steps.detail: Narrow Composio's broad default scope list to what your agent actually uses, plus openid and offline_access for refresh tokens. Scopes are space-separated, and a write scope (e.g. contact_edit) already includes read access (contact_show).
gotchas: Adding scopes later means every user has to authorize again, so get the list right before you onboard users.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: In Composio, create an OAUTH2 auth config for the bexio toolkit. Enter your client ID, client secret and the chosen scopes. Composio has no managed bexio app, so this step is required.
gotchas: The bexio endpoints are auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio/protocol/openid-connect/auth and /token. The old idp.bexio.com host was shut down on 31.03.2025.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection, sign in with your bexio account, approve the scopes and make one API call (e.g. list contacts). A 'Client nicht gefunden' (client not found) page means the client ID is wrong.
gotchas: The API acts with the connecting user's bexio permissions, so a limited user gets limited data even when the scopes are granted.

steps.title: Create a separate production app
steps.detail: bexio recommends a separate client ID and secret for production. Create a second app in the portal with the production Composio callback URL and use it in your production auth config.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

steps.title: Inform bexio once commercial-use thresholds apply
steps.detail: If you run your own business model on the API and at least 5 bexio accounts are connected, notify bexio as Section 4.4 requires. Check the exact wording in the portal terms.
gotchas: This threshold comes from a community summary. Check the actual Section 4.4 text.

steps.title: (Optional) Prepare a Marketplace partner application
steps.detail: Only if you want a listing: draft the listing texts and visuals in DE, FR, IT and EN. Confirm you meet the entry requirements: at least 10 bexio customers, at least 20 active users, OIDC login, and the app in at least 2 of the 4 languages.

steps.title: (Optional) Submit the partner form and sign the agreement
steps.detail: Fill out the form on the become-a-marketplace-partner page. If accepted, the agreement includes a 25% service fee on revenue from shared users, bexio collecting payments, price parity, and you providing end-customer support.

steps.title: (Optional) Wait for Marketplace review
steps.detail: bexio reviews the application. No timeline is published. This wait does not block public OAuth use.

blockers.symptom: The user sees an error during authorization about the redirect URL
blockers.cause: The Composio callback URL is not registered on the bexio app.
blockers.fix: Add the exact Composio callback URL to the app's redirect URLs in the developer portal.

blockers.symptom: 'Something went wrong. Client nicht gefunden.' page
blockers.cause: The client ID is wrong, or belongs to a different or deleted app.
blockers.fix: Re-copy the client ID from 'App Details' into the Composio auth config.

blockers.symptom: API calls return 403 / insufficient scope after you add new tools
blockers.cause: Refreshing a token never adds scopes.
blockers.fix: Update the scopes in the auth config and have each user authorize again.

blockers.symptom: Empty or forbidden data even though the scopes were granted
blockers.cause: Access is the intersection of the granted scopes and the connecting user's bexio permissions.
blockers.fix: Connect with a bexio user who has the needed permissions.

blockers.cause: Per-minute, per-company rate limit. The number is not published.
blockers.fix: Read the RateLimit response headers and back off.

blockers.cause: The legacy IdP host was shut down on 31.03.2025.
bexio's general terms allow it to restrict API access for good cause (e.g. migrating data away to bexio's detriment, overloading infrastructure).
blockers.fix: Stay within the terms and Section 4.4, and notify bexio when the commercial thresholds apply.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for bexio, so you always need your own app from developer.bexio.com (or a bearer token for personal use only). Register Composio's callback URL as a redirect URL, paste the client ID and secret into an OAUTH2 auth config, and trim the broad default scope list to what you need. Write scopes already include read.

evidence.claim: Composio has no managed OAuth app for bexio; a self-registered bexio app is required (managed_oauth_available=false; auth configs are OAUTH2 and BEARER_TOKEN).
bexio recommends a separate app with its own client ID and secret for production, created as an additional app in the portal.
evidence.quote: Please make sure to always use a separate set of Client ID and Client Secret for production environments.

evidence.claim: Client ID and secret are shown under 'App Details' in the portal, and the secret must stay on the server.
evidence.quote: Read the client ID and client secret under 'App Details'. The secret stays on the server.

evidence.claim: The authorization endpoint is live and rejects an unknown client_id with a 'client not found' page, so credentials are validated server-side.
evidence.quote: Something went wrong. Client nicht gefunden.

evidence.claim: OIDC discovery confirms the issuer, authorization endpoint and token endpoint, and advertises PKCE code challenge methods plain and S256.
evidence.quote: "code_challenge_methods_supported": ["plain", "S256"]

evidence.claim: Documented endpoints: authorization at auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio/protocol/openid-connect/auth and token at .../protocol/openid-connect/token.
evidence.quote: Authorization endpoint https://auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio/protocol/openid-connect/auth

evidence.claim: Refresh tokens come from the offline_access scope; an offline session closes if not renewed within one year.
evidence.quote: Offline sessions will have an idle timeout of 1 year.

evidence.claim: Refreshing a token does not change the granted scopes; new scopes need a fresh authorization.
evidence.quote: Acquiring new scopes is only possible by going through the initial authorization process again.

evidence.claim: The authorization code flow requires a server-side app, since the client secret is sent at the token exchange.
evidence.quote: Your app must be server-side because during this exchange

evidence.claim: Scopes are space-separated in the authorization request; a write scope already grants read, so contact_show is not needed with contact_edit.
evidence.quote: Read access is granted automatically when a write scope is requested for a resource.

evidence.claim: The docs say to request only the scopes an app needs. The published scope table covers resources such as contacts, invoices, quotes, projects, payroll and purchase bills, plus OIDC scopes like offline_access and company_profile.
evidence.quote: Please only request the scopes that you need for your application.

evidence.claim: The OIDC metadata advertises scopes beyond the documented table, including pat_show, internal, accountant and roles. The docs do not mark any scope as restricted or review-gated.
Effective access is the intersection of granted scopes and the user's bexio permissions; the connection runs with the rights of the user who set it up.
evidence.quote: The API access happens with the user rights of the user who set up the connection to the application.

evidence.claim: No bexio-owned page classifies scopes as sensitive or restricted, or describes a scope-review step for third-party apps.
Marketplace listing requires at least 10 bexio customers among the partner's regular clientele.
evidence.quote: At least 10 bexio customers (SMEs or fiduciaries) among your regular clientele.

evidence.claim: Marketplace listing requires at least 20 active users of the app, a clearly defined target group and a user-friendly bexio integration.
evidence.quote: At least 20 active users of your app.

evidence.claim: Marketplace listing requires integration via the bexio API with OpenID Connect login, and the app must be in at least two of DE, FR, IT and EN, with listing content in all four.
evidence.quote: Integration via bexio API and OpenID Connect login.

evidence.claim: The partner agreement has no annual fee or listing cost, but bexio takes a 25% service fee on revenue from shared users; the fee drops to 20% for the top 20% of partners by revenue.
evidence.quote: we charge a service fee of 25% on the revenue generated with shared bexio users.

evidence.claim: Applying to become a marketplace partner is done through a submission form, and no review timeline is published.
evidence.quote: Simply fill out the form so that we can get to know your solution better

evidence.claim: The partner agreement makes the partner responsible for direct support to end customers, because bexio does not support partner solutions directly.
evidence.quote: bexio does not offer direct support for partner solutions

evidence.claim: The partner agreement requires listing content (texts, visuals, optional YouTube video) in all four languages.
evidence.quote: supporting visual materials in all four languages, and optionally a video provided as a YouTube link.

evidence.claim: Developer setup starts with a bexio account: sign up for a trial at bexio.com if needed, then log into the developer portal with bexio credentials.
evidence.quote: Go to the developer portal at https://developer.bexio.com and log in using your bexio credentials.

evidence.claim: No install cap or user limit for unreviewed or unlisted apps was found in any bexio-owned page.
bexio can restrict API access for any or all customers at any time for good cause, such as data migration to bexio's detriment or infrastructure overload.
evidence.quote: restrict access to the Provider's API for any or all Customers at any time for good cause

evidence.claim: Rate limits are per minute and per company; a third-party summary says the numeric limit is not published, and a 429 response includes RateLimit headers.
evidence.quote: the API limits requests per minute and company.

evidence.claim: A third-party integrator states that bexio's per-minute rate limit is not published.
evidence.quote: Currently, the limit is not published.

evidence.claim: The docs changelog records a rate limiting section added in 2023 that explains the RateLimit HTTP headers.
evidence.quote: Added rate limiting section that explains RateLimit HTTP headers.

evidence.claim: Personal access tokens are for personal use; an app that shares access with another party must use the Authorization Code Flow.
evidence.quote: you must use the Authorization Code Flow instead.

evidence.claim: Changelog: on 2024-10-01 the IdP URL moved to auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio and the company_profile scope was added.
evidence.quote: Changed IdP URL from https://idp.bexio.com to https://auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio Added new company_profile scope.

evidence.claim: The legacy idp.bexio.com host was decommissioned on 31.03.2025; clients must use auth.bexio.com/realms/bexio.
evidence.quote: idp.bexio.com will be decommissioned on 31.03.2025.

evidence.claim: All API usage is subject to bexio's general terms and conditions.
evidence.quote: Please note that all usage of the bexio API is subject to our general terms and conditions.

evidence.claim: Before creating an app, the developer must accept the portal terms and pay attention to the commercial-use rules in Section 4.4.
evidence.quote: please pay special attention to the commercial use regulations mentioned in Section 4.4

evidence.claim: bexio offers a non-binding 30-day free trial, which can serve as the account that owns the developer app.
evidence.quote: Start a free 30-day trial with no obligation

evidence.claim: Under the marketplace partner agreement, bexio collects payments for the partner's solution directly from bexio customers; this is the claims assignment (cession) model.
evidence.quote: you grant bexio the right to collect all payments for your solution directly

evidence.claim: The partner agreement requires price parity with bexio's other sales channels for bexio customers.
evidence.quote: the obligation to maintain price parity ensures that bexio customers always receive the same conditions

evidence.claim: The partner agreement treats OIDC login as required for marketplace partners, and the partner page describes the OIDC connection as a requirement.
evidence.quote: Connecting your software to bexio's OpenID Connect (OIDC) is required

evidence.claim: Community summary of Section 4.4: a business running its own model on the API with at least five bexio accounts connected has to inform bexio.
evidence.quote: at least five bexio accounts connected has to inform bexio

evidence.claim: bexio's Marketplace page says API access is not restricted and anyone can build an integration, so building needs no partnership.
evidence.quote: We do not restrict API access: anyone can develop an integration with bexio.

evidence.claim: The app is created in the developer portal, and the developer must define allowed redirect URLs during registration.
evidence.quote: The new bexio API platform requires to define redirect URLs during the app registration in the developer portal.

evidence.claim: An app can hold up to 10 redirect URLs, e.g. for test environments and mobile apps.
evidence.quote: Up to 10 different redirect URLs can be defined for an app

evidence.claim: Unregistered redirect URLs are refused during authorization, and the user sees an error.
evidence.quote: Unknown URLs will not be accepted during the Authorization and the user will receive an error message.

open_questions: Does bexio cap users or installs, or require manual approval, for apps that are not listed on the Marketplace? No bexio page we found says so.
The app-creation form fields and any portal-side review step could not be seen, because developer.bexio.com returned only a page title.
The exact wording of Section 4.4 is unverified. The 5-account notification threshold comes from a community summary.
No bexio page classifies scopes such as payroll_*, pat_show or internal as sensitive or restricted.
No Marketplace review timeline is published.
The numeric rate limit for OAuth apps is not published.
The add-on terms in the general terms (GTC) date from June 2022 and may predate the current Marketplace terms.
